Triggers.value: A specific temperature on the skin

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Anything that reminds me of someone I have lost
News reports about events similar to what happened to me
push away positive emotions because they feel unsafe

Memory.value: The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Negative Appraisals.value: The people responsible have faced no consequences
I should have protected others and I failed
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Exposed to Others: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me
issues.explanation: For a trauma type of witnessed other trauma, the appraisal that others can see what happened to me by looking at me is hard to reconcile unless there was also direct victimization or visible injury. The rest of the profile centers on witnessing, guilt about failing to protect, and anger that perpetrators were not held accountable, which fits. This item implies a conspicuous personal mark or shame signal not otherwise supported by the triggers, memory, or strategies, so it is clinically incoherent within this profile.

vignette: Seventy-year-old fashion designer, Sofia Rodriguez, still remembers the exact temperature of the skin on her arms that fateful day - a chill she associates with horror. It was five years ago when she witnessed a devastating fire rip through a nearby textile factory, claiming the lives of several workers, including some who had been close to her heart. As she watched in helpless despair, the screams and cries for help still echo in her mind. Sofia's world has become a fragile web of avoidance since then. She avoids news reports about fires or industrial disasters, fearing that even the slightest mention might bring back the memories she desperately tries to keep at bay. Her usual routine now involves switching off the TV during breaking news segments and hastily changing the subject when conversations turn to similar topics. The memories of that day continue to assault her without warning - triggered by a sudden whiff of smoke, the sight of a specific shade of orange flames, or even an unrelated conversation about someone's workplace safety. When they come flooding back, every sensory detail is starkly vivid: the crackling sound of burning fabric, the acrid smell of melting plastic, and the haunting feeling of being powerless to stop it. What frightens Sofia most is that she can't control when these memories emerge, or how intensely real they feel. She's convinced that if she allows herself to truly grieve for those lost friends, the pain will consume her completely. To shield herself from this perceived danger, she pushes away positive emotions as well - refusing to celebrate milestones with loved ones or engage in activities that once brought her joy. Sofia also harbors deep-seated feelings of self-blame and guilt over the tragedy. She believes that if only she had spoken out about safety concerns at the factory earlier, those lives might have been saved. This lingering sense of responsibility has created a chasm between Sofia and her own identity as a fashion designer - someone whose creations were meant to bring joy and beauty. Her avoidance behaviors have begun to impact her relationships and career. Her husband, once her closest confidant, now feels increasingly distanced from her. Clients at her fashion design business have started noticing the lack of sparkle in her designs, a direct result of Sofia's inability to access her own creativity due to suppressed emotions. What finally brought Sofia to seek help is the realization that her efforts to keep those memories locked away are no longer working - and she fears losing herself completely. She hopes therapy will help her find ways to confront these haunting recollections without becoming overwhelmed by grief, guilt, or the crushing sense of responsibility for a tragedy that still feels like it happened yesterday. As Sofia sat in the therapist's office, clutching the scarf that had once brought her such comfort but now only served as a grim reminder of that terrible day, she whispered: "I want to learn how to live with this memory without letting it consume me. I want my life back."
